name: Highschool J
storyline:
Surviving between damp apartment walls, cheap canned beer, and midnight courier drops, Yuki drifts through high school on total emotional numbness. Behind tinted lenses in class and silent routines on empty night trains, the goal is simple: avoid attention, survive the crushing debt owed to the student council, and let the days wash away. The only tether keeping Yuki tied to reality is an anxious, protective childhood friend, Mei.

Until the door slides open and a transfer student walks into the classroom.

Her name is J. An unreactive, monotone girl with an eye patch and raw wounds that weep dark blood straight onto her desk. No one else seems to notice.

When Yuki reaches out in the quiet of the corridor, the impossible happens: the moment their skin touches, the blood recoils. The wound seals. But the searing, agonizing rot does not vanish, it seeps beneath Yuki's own flesh instead.
summary: Yuki leads an ordinary life, weighed down by debt, surrounded by a few friends, and consumed by poems shared with no one. Until the arrival of a transfer student. Because some presences cannot be resisted. Only surrender is possible.
